questions.question_text: "All managers are graduates. Meena is a manager. Therefore, Meena is a graduate." This argument is:
options: Inductive, as it moves from the particular to the general
Valid and sound, as the premises are true and the conclusion follows
Invalid, as the conclusion does not follow from the premises
Valid but unsound, as one premise is false

questions.question_text: "All birds can fly. Penguins are birds. Therefore, penguins can fly." This argument is:
options: Inductive and strong, because the examples are numerous
Invalid and unsound, because the conclusion does not follow
Valid but unsound, because the first premise is false
Valid and sound, because the conclusion follows from the premises

questions.question_text: "Some doctors are teachers. All teachers are patient. Therefore, some doctors are patient." This argument is:
options: Unsound because the conclusion is false

questions.question_text: "All cats are mammals. All dogs are mammals. Therefore, all cats are dogs." This argument is:
options: Invalid, as it commits the fallacy of the undistributed middle
Valid, as both premises are true
Sound, as all the premises are true
Inductive, as it moves from particulars to a universal
questions.explanation: Shared predicate does not imply identity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of inductive reasoning?
options: The sun has risen every day so far; therefore, it will rise tomorrow.
All squares are rectangles; this is a square; therefore, it is a rectangle.
All men are mortal; Socrates is a man; therefore, Socrates is mortal.
If it rains, the road is wet; it rains; therefore, the road is wet.
questions.explanation: From observed instances to a general claim.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of deductive reasoning?
options: Most Indians like cricket; Raju is Indian; therefore, he probably likes cricket.
Three swans I saw were white; therefore, all swans are white.
All metals expand on heating; copper is a metal; therefore, copper expands on heating.
The last ten buses were late; therefore, the next will probably be late.
questions.explanation: From general to specific with certainty.

questions.question_text: An inductive argument can at best be:
options: Valid or invalid, but never strong or weak
Strong or weak, but not valid in the strict sense

questions.question_text: A deductive argument is sound when it is:
options: Valid and has all true premises
